examples.claim: Serve has LLM features: response streaming, dynamic request batching, multi-node/multi-GPU serving
examples.source: serve/index.html: 'response streaming, dynamic request batching, multi-node/multi-GPU serving'

examples.claim: 2 Summarizer replicas x max_ongoing_requests=4 -> at most 8 in flight, the 9th waits in the queue
examples.source: Arithmetic on architecture.html step 3 ('more than max_ongoing_requests requests are outstanding at each replica ... left in the queue')

examples.claim: When the controller dies Ray restarts it; HTTP/gRPC/handle requests continue, autoscaling pauses and previous metrics are lost
examples.source: architecture.html Note: 'When the controller dies, requests can still be sent ... autoscaling is paused ... all previous metrics collected are lost.'

examples.claim: The custom request router RFC came out in May 2025, when P2C was Serve's only routing method
examples.source: GitHub issue #53016: 'opened on May 14, 2025'; 'Currently there is only one way to do request router in Ray Serve (i.e. power of 2 scheduling)'

examples.claim: Anyscale's 2025-09-15 blog announced custom routing and the prefix-aware router from Ray 2.49
examples.source: anyscale.com blog: 'September 15, 2025' ... 'a prefix-aware request router, PrefixCacheAffinityRouter, in Ray 2.49'

examples.claim: In the RFC sketch the callback was named on_request_scheduled
examples.source: GitHub issue #53016 code sketch: 'def on_request_scheduled(self, pending_request, replica_id, result)'

examples.claim: A custom router is attached with @serve.deployment(request_router_class=UniformRequestRouter)
examples.source: ray 2.60 serve.deployment has no request_router_class parameter (inspect.signature lists request_router_config); running the block raises TypeError: deployment() got an unexpected keyword argument 'request_router_class'. custom-request-router.html's code uses request_router_config=RequestRouterConfig(request_router_class=...).

examples.claim: backpressure status_code may only be 503 (default) or 429; Retry-After is rounded up to whole seconds; gRPC maps to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; BackpressureConfig is alpha
examples.source: ray/serve/config.py (2.60) BackpressureConfig: '@PublicAPI(stability="alpha")', 'Must be 503 (default) or 429', 'rounded up to an integer number of seconds', 'backpressure rejections always map to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED'

examples.claim: The 2.59.0 API reference says Ctrl-C shuts down Serve on the cluster; Getting Started says it tears down the application
examples.source: serve run --help (2.60): 'If you Ctrl-C the command, it will shut down Serve on the cluster.'; getting_started.html: 'killed with Ctrl-C, which will tear down the application'

examples.claim: max_ongoing_requests defaults to 5; max_queued_requests -1 means unlimited
max_replicas default is 100 with num_replicas='auto' but 1 when autoscaling_config is written by hand
examples.source: autoscaling-guide.html Note: 'including max_replicas: 100. However, if you configure autoscaling manually ... the base default for max_replicas is 1'

examples.claim: gRPC port 9000 equals serve start's default gRPC port
HTTPOptions.middlewares is deprecated and a non-empty list raises an error
examples.source: ray/serve/config.py HTTPOptions: 'middlewares: [DEPRECATED] ... Passing a non-empty list raises an error.'

examples.claim: Ion Stoica summarises Ray as an RPC framework plus an actor framework plus an object store
examples.source: paper.lingyunyang.com notes, 'From Ion Stoica - Spark, Ray, and Enterprise Open Source': 'Ray fundamentally is an RPC framework, plus an actor framework, plus an object store'

examples.claim: Engine metric logging is on by default from Ray 2.51; log_engine_metrics=False turns it off
examples.source: llm/user-guides/observability.html: 'Engine metric logging is on by default as of Ray 2.51. To disable ... set log_engine_metrics: False'
